question: Can a species-conditioned neural head on frozen ESM-2 35M features improve MIC regression under peptide-component holdout, and what is the cost of simultaneous uncertainty coverage across a whole component?
dataset: All eligible GRAMPA rows at a pinned public commit; canonical sequences 8-100 residues, finite log10-MIC targets and organism metadata
dataset_size: Use all eligible rows; no small-data ceiling or random row downsampling
representation: Frozen ESM-2 35M residue mean, amino-acid composition/length and six inherited modification flags
model: Three Gaussian-NLL MLP heads, species embeddings, AdamW, max 40 epochs, early stopping on validation NLL
split: Connected components of normalized edit similarity >=0.8; group shuffle into train/validation/calibration/test; every sequence and component stays in one split
selection: Train normalization/vocabulary only; select neural epochs on validation; compute interval multipliers on calibration; no test-driven tuning
uncertainty: Compare row residual quantile with maximum residual per calibration component; report both row and simultaneous component coverage
status: Locally fixed before fitting; not externally preregistered
limitations: Upstream processed targets omit original censoring. Data rows are not independent experiments. Edit components are not certified homology clusters. There is no publication-held-out or prospective validation claim. A worse-than-baseline result will remain in the report.
